messages.subject: Imputation in tidyLPA
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

For my master thesis in educational psychology I am doing a latent profile analysis with the tidylpa package which produced promising results. However, as I might want to use the results to write a journal article I would love to better understand the imputation mechanism in place when using single_imputation() as described in the vignette. What kind of imputation is happening - does this use the mean value for missing values or how are data points imputed?
Would be great if you could provide a detailed explanation of how the imputation is conducted in order for me to understand my results better.

Thanks and best
Lisa Weik

messages.subject: Re: Imputation in tidyLPA
messages.body_plain:
You will find your answers in the function documentation. Run ?tidyLPA::single_imputation which will take you to ?mclust::imputeData which will refer you to ?mix::imp.mix and the book by Schafer, J. L. (1996) Analysis of Incomplete Multivariate Data. Chapman \& Hall, Chapter 9.

messages.subject: TidyLPA
messages.body_plain:
Dear Joshua M. Rosenberg,

Hopefully, you can help me with some questions regarding the R package tidyLPA.  First of all, my name is Denise Blom and I am a PhD student in Health psychology at University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG) in the Netherlands. I have been working with your package for quite some time already but I got some problems/questions with the performance of this package on my current data.

I used estimate_profiles() to perform LPA. In order to get multiple fit indices, I used get_fit(). This all works fine without any warnings. However, as you can see in the attached document, the values of loglikelihood and ICL are in red. Can you explain to me why this is the case? Is there something going wrong with the estimation of the indices?
Furthermore, on many indices and based on interpretation of the clusters we would conclude that the 2 cluster solution would be optimal. However, the BLRT is very high for this cluster solution (although the p-value is significant). Can you explain to me how this value can be this high for the 2 cluster solution and not for the other solutions?

If you have any relevant literature for me that might answer my questions, that would be great!

Thank you in advance.

Kind regards,
Denise Blom
